# DIY-QuantiFluorONE-dsDNA-Fluorometer Workshop Booklet {.unnumbered}

**Prepared for the SHARK-Seq Project (2026–2027)**

**eDNA Workshop 2026**  
with Dr. Achim Meyer

## About this booklet

This booklet provides the practical and technical documentation for the DIY-QuantiFluorONE-dsDNA-Fluorometer used in the 2026 eDNA workshop within the SHARK-Seq Project.

The complete project repository, including hardware files, software, calibration tools, validation data, references, and editable documentation, is available on GitHub [@birkicht_diy_qfo_repository].

SHARK-Seq contributes to more inclusive ocean observation and demonstrates the potential of on-site sequencing as an introduction to eDNA workflows. Library construction and data processingshare steps with traditional illumina based eDNA workflows while being more robust andbioinformatically lighter, with immediate results. A side aspect is the flowcell reuse strategy whichlikewise benefits biodiversity monitoring in particular in data-poor regions: Short-fragment eDNAamplicons, which rapidly block sequencing pores, are run first; the flowcell is then flushed andreloaded with long-amplicon reference sequences efficiently utilising the remaining ~50-200 pores,substantially reducing costs.
The Then lab currently implements traditional eDNA surveys in the same region using MiFishamplicons (Illumina/Sterivex), providing benchmarks for SHARK-Seq. Additionally, Then and Meyersecured ONT funding for whole-genome sequencing of the critically endangered Bornean guitarfish(Rhinobatos borneensis, 20× coverage) on site, creating synergies for consumables and data. SHARK-Seq funds transforms the Then lab into a regional nanopore eDNA hub whilst equipping Thai andIndonesian partners with skills, seeding south–south capacity exchange.This capacity is important as climate-driven range shifts in elasmobranchs necessitate adaptivemonitoring. Rapid, cost-effective eDNA assessment enables responsive governance such as MPA boundary adjustments and fisheries regulations as species distributions change. SHARK-Seq creates a transferable model adaptable to other taxa and geographies, offering a scalable blueprint for inclusive biodiversity monitoring aligned with OBON and Global South priorities.

This booklet covers the theoretical background, hardware and mechanical design, software installation, calibration workflow, measurement protocol, quality-control procedures, analytical validation, troubleshooting, and the information required to reproduce and operate the FluoroQuant instrument (by M. Birkicht) for the dsDNA quantification.

## Current content status

This booklet documents the current validated configuration of the DIY-QuantiFluorONE-dsDNA-Fluorometer.

The documented hardware, mechanical components, firmware, calibration workflow, measurement procedure, and analytical validation correspond to the repository version supplied with this booklet.

Any future changes to hardware, firmware, optical components, calibration procedures, or analytical performance should be documented explicitly and evaluated before being treated as equivalent to the configuration described here.
